title: Partition, Prompt, Aggregate: Statistical Self-Consistency in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2607.15277v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often used to perform a form of conditional inference. In-context learning is one implicit way to do this. The prompt specifies a context and the model's output is treated as an estimate of the corresponding conditional distribution. If this interpretation holds, then LLM estimates should satisfy basic probabilistic identities. In particular, the law of total probability asserts that prior-weighted conditional distributions aggregate into population-level marginals over any valid partition of the population. In this work, we investigate to what extent LLM estimates adhere to this self-consistency principle. We use binary trees as an evaluation scaffold to recursively partition a population into increasingly fine-grained subpopulations. translated_title: 划分、提示、聚合：语言模型中的统计自洽性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）常被用于执行某种形式的条件推断，而上下文学习是实现这一目标的一种隐式方式：提示词指定一个上下文，模型的输出则被视为相应条件分布的估计。如果这种解释成立，那么LLM的估计应当满足基本的概率恒等式。特别是，全概率定律断言：在总体的任何有效划分下，以先验加权的条件分布能够聚合为总体层面的边缘分布。在本工作中，我们研究了LLM的估计在多大程度上遵循这一自洽性原则。我们使用二叉树作为评估框架，将一个总体递归地划分为粒度越来越细的子总体；然后我们用言语化的子总体描述作为上下文来提示LLM，将所得到的估计重新聚合为总体层面的估计，并对它们进行比较……
tldr: 该论文提出“划分—提示—聚合”的评估框架，利用二叉树递归划分总体，检验大语言模型给出的条件估计是否满足全概率定律所要求的统计自洽性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a "Partition, Prompt, Aggregate" evaluation framework that uses binary trees to recursively partition a population and test whether LLM estimates satisfy the statistical self-consistency required by the law of total probability.
